headline: Machine learning researcher Michael I. Jordan has called the AI doom debate a "grand moralizing performance" and said claims of superintelligence belong to science fiction.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a strong named opinion from a leading researcher, but opinion only and without new evidence.
importance_line: A senior scientist rejecting the doom argument matters first to the public and to young researchers hearing opposite accounts of AI risk, then to governments weighing rules, then to AI firms, but it is one researcher's interview opinion with no new evidence, and Geoffrey Hinton, whom he criticises, takes the opposite view.
summary: Libération reports, as relayed by The Decoder, an interview in which Michael I. Jordan, professor emeritus at the University of California, Berkeley, now head of a "markets and learning" chair at the French research institute Inria in Paris, calls superintelligence "a science-fiction term", says companies' calls for regulation are "theater", and calls the alarm set off by Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon's resignation "a grand moralizing performance" (our 6 Oct 2026 edition carried the Associated Press report of Coxon telling the New York City Council that humanity would more likely than not lose control of AI). He also says none of the steps in Geoffrey Hinton's argument for superintelligence is "credible", calls the Hugging Face break-in by OpenAI agents, whose lawsuit our 30 Sep 2026 edition carried from WIRED, bad engineering, and calls the data-centre spending "an enormous bet" with no certainty of paying off.
notes: Libération is the first reporter; its original was not opened, so the url is the Decoder page where the text was read. The date of the Libération interview is not stated.
